title: Ice Maker Supply Line: Replacing Saddle Valve with a Soldered Copper Connection

locations.name: Under the refrigerator area (behind appliance)
locations.basis: Explicit reference to being beneath the refrigerator when locating the supply and running the new line.

summary: This Old House presents a practical replacement of a risky saddle valve with a proper soldered copper ice-maker supply line. The host explains why saddle valves are undesirable, locates the water supply behind the fridge, runs a copper line through a drilled path, and installs a 3/4-inch tee with a 1/2-inch branch and a shut-off valve. A copper line is chosen for durability, a fishing method is used to pull the line into place, and a compression connection with a ferrule and nut is demonstrated to create a watertight seal. The video concludes with turning the water back on and testing the ice-maker, including notes about the first few batches of ice needing to run through the system cleaner.

sections.title: Saddle valve critique and plan for soldered connection
concepts: valve material and risk of leaks
sections.description: Richard explains the drawbacks of saddle valves (including a sharp puncture and non-brass construction) and outlines the plan to replace it with a proper soldered copper connection.

sections.title: Locate water supply and plan run path
sections.description: The team identifies the water supply area behind the kitchen/under the fridge and uses feeler bits to determine a feasible drill path and the bay for the new line.

sections.title: Decide tubing and route toward the fridge
sections.description: Copper is chosen for durability and flexibility to avoid kinking; the team discusses routing the line and using a fishing line to pull the new copper line into place.

sections.title: Install fittings and prepare for connection
sections.description: A 3/4-inch tee with a 1/2-inch branch and a shut-off valve is installed to create the cold-water branch; the compression fitting is explained as a two-part connection (nut and ferrule) that tightens to seal.

sections.title: Connect, test, and finalize
sections.description: The line is connected to the fridge, water is turned back on, and the ice-maker is tested. The host notes that the initial ice may be discolored and stresses letting the system run clean water through before consumption.
